title: Mirror Luka
description: Get reflected and you're pulled into the mirror. A top-down stealth puzzle about sneaking through a cursed mansion
detailedFeatures:
A top-down stealth puzzle made for a one-day game jam with the theme "utsuru" (to be reflected).

If a mirror reflects you, you get pulled into the world inside it. Luka, a girl who wandered into an old mansion deep in the forest on a dare, finds that every mirror in the house is cursed to swallow whatever it reflects.

In front of each mirror, a faintly glowing "reflection zone" lies on the floor. Avoid it and make your way to the exit door! Hide behind pillars, bookshelves or sofas and the mirrors can't see you.
technologies: Python（サウンド・アイコン生成）

title: Kiwa -際-
description: Two players take turns pouring tea into one cup. Spill it and you lose.
detailedFeatures:
A two-player duel built for a game jam whose theme, "kasa", I read as "kasa" meaning volume — the rising level of liquid in a single cup.

A tea room at night, one cup on the tatami. The two players pour in turns, and whoever makes it overflow loses that round. First to two rounds wins.

[Rules]
Tea flows only while you hold the button and stops the moment you let go. On your turn you must pour at least a drop — passing is not allowed. The "kiwa" (the brink) is not a hidden number: it is the rim of the cup itself, so the limit is always in plain sight. Pour a little and you stay safe but leave your opponent room; pour a lot and you corner them, but you carry the risk of spilling yourself.

The vessel changes every round (sake cup, soba cup, teacup, tea bowl). The pouring speed is constant, so capacity translates directly into "how long until the rim", and last round's instincts no longer apply. Before each duel a kagetsu card is drawn to decide who pours first.

You can also play alone, handing the second hand to one of three NPCs — an old monk, a travelling performer, a samurai. Since the brink is visible to everyone, the only difference is where they stop. Each has its own target level, hand tremor and hesitation time, producing cautious, capricious and bold styles.

[Architecture]
Layered as platform -> infrastructure -> game -> core, with the gameplay itself (core + game) never touching DxLib or any OS API. To keep an iOS release open, the entry point and font registration are confined to a handful of files in the platform layer. Duel rules live in the Model, drawing in the View, and randomness and presentation glue in the Presenter — no randomness is allowed inside the Model.

The 3D vessels, teapot, textures and icon are generated by Python scripts, with the vessel dimensions shared between the view's formula and the script.
myResponsibilities: A solo project, so I handled the concept, design and implementation entirely. I focused on isolating the DxLib dependency behind a layered architecture, separating Model / View / Presenter, designing the NPCs' playing styles, and building the Python pipeline that generates the 3D models and textures.
technologies: レイヤードアーキテクチャ
supportedPlatforms: Download the zip and run the exe

title: Kodama
description: A 2D action game where you "see" a pitch-black cave through ripples of sound
detailedFeatures: A 2D action game for iOS, built by a team of three at CyberAgent's "Proto Sprint League" internship. The screen is almost entirely dark, and all you can do is tap to jump. Landing sends out a ripple of sound, and only the blocks it touches light up for an instant, revealing the terrain.
myResponsibilities: I was in charge of the rendering and the staging around it, aiming to make the moment of landing feel fun and satisfying for the player. Since the game is set inside a cave, I also implemented the sound so that it feels like it echoes off the walls.
award: Proto Sprint League 2026 — Award of Excellence

title: WIN vs MAC
description: A 3D action RPG where you fight through a dungeon inside Windows, using your own PC as a weapon.
detailedFeatures: You play as a digital entity inside Windows, fighting your way to the final boss: a MacBook. Its defining feature is that the machine you are actually running on becomes part of the game. The title screen renders live CPU, memory and disk usage as its background graph, and the loadout screen is a Windows-desktop-style UI (WebView2 + HTML/CSS/JS) where you equip real files from your own PC. The extension of the file you pick changes your stats (.cpp raises critical rate, .mp4 extends projectile range, and so on), difficulty selection is styled as a UAC dialog, and results appear as a shutdown screen on victory or a blue screen on defeat. Combat is 3D action with melee combos, window-throwing projectiles, charged shots and deflection; enemies are Mac-side processes (Safari, Xcode) plus the phase-based MacBook boss. Enemy behaviour is data-driven — defined by combining behaviors/animations in JSON rather than by subclassing. Architecturally the project uses strict layering (Platform → Infrastructure → Game → Core) with an ECS inside the Game layer, an EventBus for loosely coupled systems, and interface-only access to DxLib and the Windows API.
myResponsibilities: Solo project — I handled planning, architecture, implementation, asset production and balancing myself. My main focus areas were the layered architecture with an ECS game layer, decoupling systems through an EventBus, making enemy AI data-driven via JSON behaviour/animation composition, pulling live system metrics from the Windows API and building the OS-style UI with WebView2, and establishing an AI-generated model → Mixamo → mv1 animation pipeline.
supportedPlatforms: Download the zip and run the exe

title: CodeTree (Git Tool)
description: A Windows Git client that combines SourceTree's Git workflow with VS Code's development experience.
detailedFeatures: AI commit-message generation sends staged diffs to the Claude API and proposes messages in Conventional Commits format. Prefixes such as feature/ and fix/ can be entered with one click, and custom prefixes can also be registered. Clicking a changed filename jumps directly to its diff, while Compact Mode provides a space-saving view focused on frequently used actions. The app also includes a commit graph, branch and stash management, GitHub integration, a statistics dashboard, and an integrated PowerShell terminal.
myResponsibilities: Handled planning, architecture design, and class design. Implementation was delegated to AI.

title: V-Link Battle
description: A VTuber battle game created on campus. First long-term, large-scale project.
detailedFeatures: A game where VTubers battle on a live streaming stage. The main focus was on comments. Initially, I used TMP to scroll text, but it lacked depth and didn't utilize the 3D space effectively. So I created a Python tool to generate 3D models from input text, executed it in Blender to create them in batch, and replaced the system to play them back. The result looked much better. I also created special comments and gimmicks that only work because of live streaming. At the time, I was still inexperienced with Unity, so I struggled with 3D model display and rendering.

title: Yamikin Girl Jirai-chan
description: A 2D wire-action game born at the Bandai Namco Studios Cup, polished up and heading to Steam
detailedFeatures:
A 2D wire-action game in development for Steam. We rebuilt "Shin-layer Shin-ri Mine-chan", the entry from the two-week Bandai Namco Studios Cup game jam, moving it from C++/Siv3D to Unity 6.

Control Yumemi and make full use of her wire to defeat enemies and swing between platforms on the way to each goal. Clear every area and escape from this world.

[Game System]
Each area pairs an action part focused on clearing the stage with a story part that follows it. As you progress, novel-style scenes gradually bring you closer to the truth of this world, so you can enjoy the setting more deeply.

[Story]
Yumemi, an amnesiac "jirai-kei" girl, wakes up in a nightmarish world. Before her appears Risuka, a mysterious being that looks like a stuffed toy. To return home she must defeat the bosses lurking in the depths of the psyche and collect the "yami-kin". Relying on the wire in her choker, Yumemi sets out to collect them all and escape.

[Technical Work on My Parts]
- Block gimmicks: a single MonoBehaviour holds a list of IBlockAbility, so moving, damaging, paired and wire-pullable blocks are composed instead of subclassed and can be mass-produced just by combining prefabs.
- Config screen: split into Presenter / View and kept alive in the manager scene, decoupling "pause" from "open settings". Values persist to PlayerPrefs, covering volume, graphics, aim assist and gamepad sensitivity in one place.
- Camera: unified follow, shake and zoom behind an ICameraEffect interface on Cinemachine 3; hits trigger shake through the EventBus, and FOV is interpolated with the player's speed while swinging to sell the sense of momentum.
myResponsibilities: Design and implementation of the block gimmicks (moving, damaging, paired and wire-pullable blocks), the config screen (saving and applying volume, graphics and assist settings), and the Cinemachine-based camera (follow, shake, zoom, speed-linked FOV)

title: Takashi, Betting on Life
description: 2D shooting game developed in 3 days during school game jam. Led a team of 5. Won Horikawa Award from Infinite Loop Inc.
detailedFeatures:
This game was created during a 3-day in-school game jam. As the project leader for my first game jam, managing the team was challenging.
It was a great learning experience coordinating with designers on the type of artwork needed and the format. With many programmers on the team, creating base classes and shortening the critical path was quite difficult.
I was just starting to learn design patterns, so I worked hard on optimization using Singleton, ObjectPool, and other patterns.
myResponsibilities: Project Leader, Base Class Design, Singleton Pattern Implementation, ObjectPool System Implementation
award: Horikawa Award from Infinite Loop Inc.

Learning from the previous internal game jam, I prepared the Unity project and base classes in advance, and set up repository integration before the event.
While the game was completed successfully, we couldn't achieve a satisfying result. So we polished it several times and displayed it at SAPPORO GAME ODYSSEY. It was well-received, so based on the feedback, we decided to further refine it and release on Steam.
myResponsibilities: Base class design, player bullet implementation, enemy behavior & attack pattern implementation, ranking feature addition, Steam store page creation, etc.
